title: Players
summary: Manages every connected player: join/leave events (PlayerAdded/PlayerRemoving), the player list (GetPlayers), and client-side access to the local player (LocalPlayer).

methods.name: GetPlayers
methods.description: Array of every Player currently in the game.

methods.name: GetPlayerFromCharacter
methods.description: Given a character model, returns its Player (or nil).

methods.name: GetPlayerByUserId
methods.description: Finds an in-game player by UserId.

methods.name: GetHumanoidDescriptionFromUserId
methods.description: Fetches a user's avatar description (yields; server only).

events.name: PlayerAdded
events.description: Fires when a player joins. On the server this is where you load data, set up leaderstats, etc.

events.name: PlayerRemoving
events.description: Fires just before a player leaves — the standard save hook.

properties.name: LocalPlayer
properties.description: Client only. The Player object of the person running this client. Nil on the server.

properties.name: RespawnTime
properties.description: Seconds until a dead player respawns.

explanation.whatItIs: The service in charge of people: who's here, who joined, who left, and (on the client) who YOU are.
explanation.whyItExists: Multiplayer games live and die by join/leave handling — data loading, leaderstats, cleanup all hang off these events.
whenToUse: Server: PlayerAdded → load data / create leaderstats; PlayerRemoving → save data
Server: loop GetPlayers() for round logic
Client: Players.LocalPlayer for your own player object
Mapping characters back to players: GetPlayerFromCharacter
whenNotToUse: Don't access Players.LocalPlayer in Scripts (server) — it's nil there
Don't assume PlayerAdded already fired for existing players when your script starts — iterate GetPlayers() first
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
SERVER                              CLIENT
Players.PlayerAdded  (every join)   Players.LocalPlayer (you)
Players.PlayerRemoving (every leave) Players:GetPlayers() (who you see)
Players:GetPlayers()  (authoritative)
```
tips: Classic join-handler shape: handle existing players with GetPlayers(), THEN connect PlayerAdded
Character spawning is separate: listen to player.CharacterAdded for per-spawn setup
leaderstats is a convention: a Folder named 'leaderstats' parented to the Player shows on the leaderboard
commonMistakes: Missing early joiners: connecting PlayerAdded after some players already joined
Saving only on PlayerRemoving — server crashes lose that data; also save periodically
Confusing Player (the account object) with Character (the physical model, which respawns)

examples.title: The canonical join/leave skeleton
examples.code:
local Players = game:GetService("Players")

local function onPlayerAdded(player)
    -- leaderstats (convention: Folder named "leaderstats")
    local stats = Instance.new("Folder")
    stats.Name = "leaderstats"
    local coins = Instance.new("IntValue")
    coins.Name = "Coins"
    coins.Value = 0
    coins.Parent = stats
    stats.Parent = player

    player.CharacterAdded:Connect(function(character)
        print(player.Name .. " spawned")
    end)
end

-- Handle players who joined BEFORE this script ran:
for _, player in Players:GetPlayers() do
    task.spawn(onPlayerAdded, player)
end
-- ...and everyone after:
Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(onPlayerAdded)

Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player)
    print(player.Name .. " left — save their data NOW")
end)
